summary: thread the analytic validation forward across 2 threads (THREAD_MIN split)
comment: REGRESSION 0.9438 under --processes 10, though single-user profile showed it FASTER (user37 1385->1272). Cause: memory-bandwidth contention. Validation forward is forward-ONLY = memory-bound (few transcendentals per array read); under 10 parallel workers the mem subsystem is saturated, so the 2nd thread just waits on memory + adds spawn overhead -> net slower. Contrast iter3 grad-threading (accepted 1.08x): fwd+bwd is compute-bound enough to hide mem latency. LESSON: single-user profiler MISLEADS on threading; only --processes 10 is truth. Parallelism is SMT-capped AND bandwidth-capped -> pivot to WORK-REDUCTION (ln-cache, dummy-bwd removal), not more threads. Reverted analytic.rs to iter6 single-threaded batch_loss. Was bit-for-bit (threaded sum didn't flip any best-epoch).

summary: rewrite 12 forward powf as exp(e*ln), cache the ln, reuse in backward
comment: Microbench (profiling/bench_powf.rs): powf=11.5ns vs exp=4.5ns vs ln=5.2ns -> powf~2.5x exp. Rewrote each forward base.powf(exp) as (exp*ln_base).exp() in curve_fwd/stab_fwd (12 sites), cached ln_base in CurveCache(+6: ln_sf shared by p35&p31, ln_b1,ln_b2,ln_s,ln_w27,ln_w28)/StabCache(+3: ln_ls,ln_ld,ln_ls1), reused in curve_bwd/stab_bwd to KILL the backward's 13 ln/timestep recomputes. Net: powf->exp(cheap) + ln moved fwd(reused not extra). grad 0.565->0.454(-20%), valid 0.497->0.436(-12%, fwd-only also gains via cross-site ILP). Precision-trading(3b): d_AVG -0.000091, 21/50 params drift(FP reorder, expected). WORK-reduction so HELD under --processes 10 (contrast iter7 threading=bandwidth-bound). Cumulative drift vs orig baseline 0.309825 now +0.000113(improved from +0.000204). grad_matches_fd passes. cached ln is f32(matches f32 fwd); bwd casts to f64.

summary: share ln(last_s/last_sf/last_d) across curve + both stability traces; 3 fewer ln per timestep (bit-for-bit)

summary: thread SIMD gradient across 2 cores (split card-groups) - REJECTED, vector units SMT-saturated
comment: REJECTED: speed_ratio 0.6229 (38% REGRESSION). Bit-for-bit correct (0/50 param diff, d_AVG 0.000000) - purely a speed loss. Split the 8-card groups across 2 thread::scope threads (mirroring iter3's scalar-grad threading, THREAD_MIN_GROUPS=8). KEY FINDING: this is the OPPOSITE of iter3. The f32x8 forward SATURATES the physical core's vector/SIMD execution units with ONE thread, so the worker's 2nd pinned CPU (an SMT sibling sharing those same vector units) adds NO vector throughput - only thread spawn/join overhead per batch. iter3's SCALAR grad helped from threading because scalar units were underutilized and SMT could overlap them; vectorized work can't (SIMD units are the bottleneck and already full). To use the idle 2nd core would need coarser-than-per-batch parallelism (epochs are sequential due to weight updates; a persistent pool's per-batch sync would likely also dominate now that each batch-grad is ~0.6ms). NOT worth the complexity. LESSON for the campaign: once a phase is SIMD-vectorized, threading it on an SMT sibling is a dead end - the 2 levers (SIMD width, SMT threads) compete for the same vector units, they don't stack. Reverted analytic.rs to single-thread batch_loss_and_grad_simd (kept an explanatory comment documenting this). champion stays iter15 (170ms median this session). NEXT: lower-degree exp8 for the grad (precision-trade ~5-8%), or the O(N^2)->O(N) window (big, needs care).

summary: Minimax (Remez) exp8 deg 6->4 and ln8 deg 4->2: 4 fewer FMAs
comment: iter17 ACCEPT. exp8: degree-6 Taylor -> degree-4 RELATIVE-minimax (Remez, rel err 2.6e-6); ln8: t^9 atanh series -> degree-2-in-u minimax (abs err 4.9e-6). Coeffs from profiling/minimax_coeffs.py (mpmath Remez). speed_ratio 1.1557 median, mean 1.1549 (broad, no single user carrying), d_AVG LogLoss -0.000000 (champ 0.310071 vs cand 0.310070 -> essentially zero; 49/50 params reordered, max param diff 2.04, but Adam lands equally good = precision-trade ruling confirmed). max per-user dLL 0.0023 (diagnostic only). complexity 6458->6460 (+2 from doc comments, removed poly terms nearly offset; ratio 1.0003, threshold 1.0008, passes hugely). WHY +15.6pct not the predicted ~7pct: the FSRS forward is a SEQUENTIAL recurrence, so each transcendental Horner chain sits on the LATENCY critical path -- cutting chain links (exp 6->4, ln 4->2 terms) cuts latency directly, far more than throughput op-count suggested. KEY LESSON: transcendental Horner-chain DEPTH is a real lever on the serial recurrence. The 6.7e-6 worst-case in simd_transcendentals_accurate is the f32 range-reduction floor (x-n*ln2 cancellation near x~88), pre-existing, NOT the poly; gated at 1e-5. Scalar oracle still uses libm exp/ln; cross-checks (simd_grad_matches_scalar_grad etc.) still passed at 2e-3. champion now 8733878a064d (was a1c5aeda3a70 iter15). NEXT: could push exp8->deg3/ln8->deg1 but accuracy 7.5e-5 risks band over compounding -- diminishing. Bigger remaining bet = O(N^2)->O(N) expanding window.

summary: O(N) expanding window: one per-card pass scores every timestep, replacing O(N^2) per-prefix forward
comment: iter18 ACCEPT - THE WINDOW BET (biggest single win). O(N^2)->O(N) expanding window. A card with K reviews was K-1 prefix-items (lengths 2..K) each re-running its whole prefix recurrence = O(K^2) timestep-work; now each card is ONE column whose recurrence runs ONCE over its full review sequence, scoring a BCE loss at every timestep t>=1. KEY IDENTITY: the curve curve8_fwd(state_{t-1}, delta_t[t]) step8_fwd computes for review t's stability update IS the prediction R_t (same input state + same delta_t), so a loss is read off every step for free. The per-step loss adjoint is injected into step8_bwd via a NEW g_r_loss param -> curve8_bwd(g_r_a+g_r_b+g_r_loss); the O(N^2) callers pass 0 (bit-for-bit no-op). NEW analytic.rs: card_loss_and_grad_simd (grad; loss value skipped since training discards it), card_loss_simd (validation), Step8::curve_out helper, scalar O(N) oracle loss_and_grad_range_window (test-only, separate curve_bwd for the loss adjoint - linear so equals the SIMD single-call). training.rs: BatchHost.windowed flag, build_batch_host_windowed (re-group prefix-items by card, longest prefix = full seq, place weight/label at t=reviews.len()-1), train() + validation branch on hb.windowed; benchmark()/evaluate() keep the plain per-prefix path. MIN prefix length is 2 (the empty-history item predicting the first review is dropped by df[delta_t>0]), so windowed t=0 is pure init, never a loss. TWO-PHASE DE-RISK: Phase-1 probe (card-grouped batching but KEPT the slow per-prefix forward) gave the EXACT training trajectory at +0.000912 vs iter17 -> Andrew EXPANDED band to absolute +-0.0015 = [0.3083,0.3113]. VALIDATION (all pass): cargo window_grad_equals_sum_of_prefix_grads (THE math identity: windowed grad == sum of per-prefix grads, rel-L2<1e-9) + simd_window_grad_matches_scalar_window (rel-L2<2e-3); Phase-2 params match Phase-1 probe (34/50 BIT-identical, rest FP-reassoc; mean LL 0.310912 vs probe 0.310982); band 0.310912 in [0.3083,0.3113] (~0.0002 headroom under 0.3113); plain benchmark() BIT-FOR-BIT (diff of result jsonl IDENTICAL vs champion re-run => g_r_loss=0 truly a no-op). speed_ratio 3.1182 median, mean 3.3957. complexity 6460->7207 (ratio 1.1156, thr 1.3146 << 3.1182). champion .pyd 1be0802a170065b0. d_AVG vs champ +0.000842 (the Phase-1 card-grouping cost, expected). KEEP the scalar O(N^2) per-prefix kernels (loss_and_grad_range_simd/batch_loss_and_grad_simd/batch_loss_simd) - benchmark() still uses them. RE-ANCHOR NEXT: product jumped 21.0->65.5, large winner's-curse gap to close.

summary: Build host batches once (train==test): reuse for grad+validation, drop redundant clone+build
comment: iter19 ACCEPT, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50 param diff, d_AVG 0.000000). After the O(N) window collapsed the forward, the per-user SETUP FLOOR grew to ~23% (median user 37) / ~34% (large user 34) of compute_parameters() time. train() got handed weighted_train_set.clone() + weighted_train_set (train==test in BOTH compute_parameters() and benchmark()), so it cloned the whole dataset AND ran build_host_batches() TWICE on identical data (train_host + valid_host). Now train() takes ONE dataset, builds host batches ONCE, and the validation reuses train_host (only the index order differs: per-epoch reshuffle for grad vs the fixed valid_order). Drops 1 O(N) clone + 1 full build_host_batches. Bit-for-bit because grad/valid only READ the immutable batches. +14.5% median (mean 1.1464). complexity 7207->7204 (removed test_set param + valid_host build + clone; ratio 0.9996, so only the 5pct bar binds). champion .pyd was 1be0802a (iter18) -> iter19 build. RE-ANCHOR (iter18): true cumulative vs iter0 = x62.04 median (mean x71.97), cumulative LogLoss cost +0.001087 vs iter0, in band. NEXT floor ideas: build_batch_host_windowed re-groups by card via HashMap AFTER group_cards_into_batches already grouped+flattened (double work) -> have group return the per-card structure; also the validation BCE is a scalar f64 per-lane ln loop (could vectorize with ln8, but that's a precision-trade, band headroom only ~0.0004).

summary: Unified BCE -ln(1-|label-r|) (Andrew): vectorize validation ln8 + one-division gradient seed
comment: iter20 ACCEPT, ANDREW'S IDEA. Unified label-BCE identity -ln(1-|label-r|): equals -ln(r) for label 1 and -ln(1-r) for label 0. FSRS labels are always 0/1 (rating==1 -> 0 else 1), so it is exact (soft labels in (0,1) would differ, but never occur). Being BRANCHLESS it vectorizes. Applied in TWO spots of the WINDOWED path: (1) VALIDATION card_loss_simd: replaced the scalar f64 per-lane libm-ln loop with ONE f32x8 ln8 over arg=1-|lbl-r| (up to 8 scalar lns -> 1 SIMD ln). +4.4pct alone, and params stayed BIT-FOR-BIT because the f32 ln8 shifted validation loss VALUES but not the epoch RANKING -> same best epoch selected. (2) GRADIENT card_loss_and_grad_simd g_r seed: d[-ln(1-|label-r|)]/dr = -sign(label-r)/(1-|label-r|) = ONE division vs the old two (lbl/r - (1-lbl)/(1-r)); this DOES drift params (precision-trade). COMBINED: +5.9pct median (mean 1.0602), band 0.310939 in [0.3083,0.3113] (d_AVG +0.000027 vs champ; 16/50 params reordered, max param diff 0.694, max per-user dLL 0.001723). complexity 7204->7196 (vectorized validation deleted the scalar loop; ratio 0.9989, only the 5pct bar binds). LEFT the PLAIN O(N^2) path (loss_and_grad_range_simd, benchmark's) on the old two-division form so benchmark.py stays bit-for-bit. summary: Gradient skip-last (curve-only at final timestep) + cached sort-key + merged longest-prefix scan; bit-for-bit
comment: BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50 params, d_AVG 0.000000) on compute_parameters, confirmed across TWO fresh back-to-back pairs: 1.0547 and 1.0541 (logged the conservative 1.0541). Forward computes the curve ONLY at the last step (skips 2 stab + next_d + ln(last_d)); the dropped state is unused. Peeled the last step out of BOTH the fwd loop (now 0..seq_len-1) and the bwd loop, seeding (g_s,g_d,g_sf) from curve8_bwd gated by the UNCLAMPED incoming state (= s0/d0/sf0). Factored the BCE g_r adjoint into a g_r_loss_at closure (used by peel + loop). Added debug_assert seq_len>=2. WINDOWED-ONLY change so cp 0/50 fully covers it; cargo test (incl O(N^2) simd_grad_matches_scalar_grad + simd_batch_loss_matches_scalar) confirms the untouched batch/benchmark path; benchmark.py NOT rerun (provably untouched, shared kernels unchanged). summary: Per-group padding skip: each group runs only to its longest card, not the batch-wide seq_len
comment: REJECTED on the 5% floor: +4.1% median (two pairs 1.0403, 1.0412; mean 1.0504), BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50, d_AVG 0). The windowed forward ran every group to the batch-wide seq_len (= longest card in the batch); within a length-sorted batch a group of SHORTER cards then runs all-padding timesteps (every lane rating==0 = pure state passthrough, weight 0). card_loss_and_grad_simd + card_loss_simd now scan r_hist per group (reduce_add==0 detects all-pad since ratings>=0) to find the group's active length sl and run only 0..sl, moving the iter24/25 skip-last to each group's OWN last real step. No signature/plumbing change (self-detected from the data). WALL-MAPPING INSIGHT: length-sorting (group_cards_into_batches sorts by full_len) makes batches length-homogeneous, so the recoverable INTER-group padding caps ~4% for the median user (mean 5% is right-skewed: users with diverse card lengths benefit more); residual INTRA-group per-lane padding is unrecoverable (SIMD lanes step together). BANKED for a future stack-to-5% bundle: patch /tmp/iter26_skip.patch (git apply), candidate .pyd /tmp/iter26_cand.pyd c427acb5, complexity 7257->7285. Hunted hard for a >=1% bit-for-bit companion: none found (iter24 already took the exp-fusions; shared-subexpr hoists are <0.5% and would churn many call sites incl the benchmark path; div->reciprocal is a precision trade and the bands are spent). All 6 cargo tests GREEN. Will resurrect the skip when a >=1% bit-for-bit companion appears.

summary: Windowed batches built from item headers: no normalize pass, regrouping, or per-item copies
comment: ACCEPTED, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50 params, d_AVG LogLoss 0, 0.308320). Round 2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28). FSRS_PROFILE split of the setup outside the train loop (u17 130k items): normalize 3.4ms + weight/retain 2.5 + HashMap group 12.6 + build 4.0 + drop of the grouped Vec<Vec<Vec<item>>> 10.5 = ~33ms of ~137 (24%); ~15% for median users. New build_host_batches_carded: one pass over item HEADERS in input order (len, card id -> dense index via a 1-multiply hasher, recency weight) -> compact (card,t,weight) records -> counting sort by card -> sort cards by (full_len, id) -> lay out each card's longest prefix (delta_t clamped here = what normalize did; label = rating of review t of the longest prefix, since every prefix is a head of it). normalize only runs for the outlier filter / plain path. card_id field removed from WeightedFSRSItem; train() takes prebuilt host batches. KEY LESSON: reading each item's heap data in CARD order missed the cache per item (first version saved only ~5ms); header-only pass fixed it. u17 setup 33->17ms (8.5ms is now just freeing the 130k input Vecs). MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: an RWKV training job (other project, ~7 cores, ends ~9h later) loaded the box: per-user ratios spread 0.79-1.54 and the median times (21.5 vs 23.0) disagree with the ratio. Dev cross-check (single process, cached raw arrays via compute_parameters_raw, min of 21 reps/user, champ-vs-champ noise 0.4%): x1.0895 median. cand .pyd 0da2ea78 (rebuild 90752ef5, non-reproducible PE bytes), champ 1e8e2316.

summary: Stack: exp8 single-convert rounding, peel first step, drop dead/cheap cache fields
comment: ACCEPTED, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50, LogLoss 0.308320). Official 1.1010 (RWKV load); dev bench stack ~x1.14. Parts (dev bench, min of 21 reps/user, each vs the previous): (1) peel t==0 out of the forward and backward time loops (no t==0 branch in the body): +2.2%; (2) Stab8 no longer caches aa (a constant), hard/easy (recomputed from rating), ln_ls (= curve.ln_s / ln_sf) and ln_ld (NEVER read) -> the per-step ln8(last_d) that only fed that dead field disappears: +1.6%; (3) recompute cheap values in the backward instead of caching them (Step8 last_s/last_sf/last_d/ns3/nsf3, Curve8 m1/decay1/factor1/b1/weight1/weight2/wsum, Stab8 pls/ls_sinc/bb): +0.7% (the kernel is not memory-bound); (4) THE BIG ONE, +9.5%: the build target is baseline x86-64 = SSE2 only (constraint 7), where wide's f32x8::round() is convert/convert-back/compare/3-op blend and round_int() adds NaN/overflow guards, ~11 ops per half, on every exp8 (15 per step). exp8's clamp already maps NaN to -87 (maxps returns its 2nd operand), so x*LOG2E is finite and within +-128: one fast_round_int (cvtps2dq, nearest-even) + round_float gives the same n and exponent bits. Same on NEON (vcvtnq = vrndnq + convert for in-range values). LESSON: check what wide lowers to on the BASELINE target, not on AVX2. cand .pyd ceab5721, champ 865a364c.

summary: Run the SIMD kernels 4 cards per lane (f32x4) instead of 8
comment: REJECTED: slower. FIRST iteration on the PAIRED protocol (profiling/measure_paired.py): 0.9476 / 0.9526 in two runs, mean 0.951/0.964. Not bit-for-bit (50/50 params: 4-lane groups change the per-group f32 reduce order), mean LogLoss 0.308321 (+1.1e-6, in band). One oracle test (simd_batch_loss_matches_scalar, O(N^2) path tail) failed after the blind sed - moot. MOTIVATION: the asm of card_loss_and_grad_simd on the SSE2 baseline shows 2353 movaps vs 1190 mulps + 639 addps: an f32x8 value takes 2 of the 16 xmm registers, so heavy spilling. Hypothesis was that f32x4 (1 register per value, same element-wise instructions) would cut spills. Result says the spills are not the bottleneck (or per-group overhead doubles and eats it). Same asm also shows the g_r_loss_at closure is NOT inlined (a real call per step) and 46 bounds-check branches - next candidates. cand .pyd cand40x4, champ ceab5721. Reverted.

Parts (paired, 3 runs each vs the previous part): (1) g_r_loss_at closure -> #[inline(always)] fn (the asm showed a real call per step): +0.3/+1.0/+1.0%; (2) load8 = one slice bounds check instead of 8 index checks: +2.4/+1.6/+1.9%; (3) backward loop iterates caches (no per-step index check): +0.4/+0.9/+0.3%; (4) exp8_in_range = exp8 without its [-87,88] clamp for every forward call: clip_parameters bounds the weights and the states are clamped, so |arg| <= ~21 (p35/p31/cc), <= ~13 (se/ex34/qbase/pr/expr/init), e1 in [0,60] via its explicit min, r1/r2 >= -0.95*88.7 even for an overflowed +inf base; the clamp never changes a value: +2.9/+2.2/+2.9%. Parts summed ~6% but the single official stack run read 4.6% (parts measured against each other drift). Tried and dropped (not logged separately, paired dev runs): label derived from rating instead of the labels array (1.00, no kernel gain), &[f32; 34] weights to kill constant-index checks (0.99, slightly slower). cand .pyd 427158c7, champ ceab5721.

summary: iter35 stack plus: skip re-clamping already-clamped states, drop ln8's redundant exponent mask
comment: ACCEPTED, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50, LogLoss 0.308320), paired protocol one official run: 1.0706 median / 1.0741 mean. = the iter35 stack (inline g_r_loss_at fn, one-check load8, cache iterator, exp8_in_range for the proven-bounded forward exps; 1.046 alone) + (5) step8_fwd/step8_bwd/the final-step curve no longer clamp the incoming state: it is always a previous step8_fwd output, already clamped (first step clamps its init values), so last_s == s0 exactly; the gradient gates still test s0/d0/sf0: (6) ln8 drops '& 0xff' after bits >> 23 (every ln8 input is positive, sign bit 0). (5)+(6) paired vs iter35: +1.1/+2.1/+1.7%. Not done (too small / fragile): dropping the dt >= 0 fast_max calls (the builder guarantees it, but it ties the kernel to the builder for ~0.3%). cand .pyd bb32de59, champ ceab5721.

summary: Second thread shares each batch's card groups (dynamic claims), also frees the input items
comment: ACCEPTED, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50, LogLoss 0.308320), paired one official run 1.0858 median / 1.1239 mean (complexity +1.5% -> bar 1.038). Constraint 2 allows 2 threads/user. SMT probe first (smt_test: 6 users x10 on CPU 30 alone 1.46 s; two copies on SMT siblings 30+31 2.40 s each = 1.22x combined throughput; separate cores ~2x): the official setup pins each worker to one core's 2 SMT threads, so the ceiling here is ~1.22x, while a real Anki machine would usually give the thread its own core. Design (GradShared in training.rs): one scoped helper per train() call (it first drops the prefix-items = the old drop thread, so never >2 threads); per windowed batch the main thread publishes w + batch index, both threads claim 8-card groups (longest first) through one AtomicU64 = (job seq << 32 | next group), so a late thread cannot claim from a new job; each group's f32 lane sums go to out[g]; the main thread adds out[0..n] IN GROUP ORDER = exactly the one-thread f64 sum. Spin waits (batches ~26 us, OS wakeups too slow). analytic.rs: card_loss_and_grad_simd split into card_group_grad (one group -> [f32;34]) + a single-thread loop (tests). Pre-inlining iter16 (0.62x) spawned threads per batch; this keeps one thread for the whole call. Noise note: the two-thread binary's own reps spread more under the RWKV background load (e.g. u44 8.4/15.5/10.3 ms); three dev paired runs read 1.19/1.10/1.08. cand .pyd bfb87d05, champ bb32de59.

summary: exp8: add n to the polynomial's exponent bits instead of multiplying by 2^n
comment: REJECTED: no gain. Paired runs 0.9949 / 0.9972 / 0.9997 (mean 0.992/0.998/1.010), BIT-FOR-BIT 0/50. For the proven-bounded forward exps (x >= -84 -> n >= -121, poly in [0.7, 1.42]) p*2^n is always a normal float, so bits(p) + (n << 23) is exactly the product's bits and saves one op (the +127 and the float multiply become one integer add). The clamped exp8 kept the multiply (subnormal results near -87). One op of ~14 per exp is below the noise, and paddd on float data may add a domain-crossing delay. Timing medians not recorded for this run (~12 ms both sides). champ bfb87d05. Reverted.

summary: Helper lays out batches in training order; no per-step clock reads, allocations, dead penalty value
comment: ACCEPTED, BIT-FOR-BIT (0/50, LogLoss 0.308320). Paired one official run 1.0516 median / 1.0507 mean (complexity +0.9% -> bar 1.022); n=1 CHECK (new rule, bench_min single process pinned to 2 CPUs, 3 rounds): 1.0209 median / 1.0262 mean -> passes. Parts (paired, 3 runs each): (1) lazy layout: compute_parameters only PLANS the windowed batches (CardedPlan: hash pass, counting sort, card sort, bounds; no powf) and train() holds batches in OnceLock slots; its helper thread owns the prefix-items, lays the batches out in epoch 1's shuffle order (same seeded RNG, cloned), computing each recency weight there, then frees the items and joins the group sharing; the main thread waits only for the first batch: 1.030/1.035/1.040 (n=1 1.019); (2) Adam without per-step allocations (borrow w instead of clone, clip_parameters_in_place): ~+0.3%; (3) the 6 Instant::now clock reads per Adam step ran even without FSRS_PROFILE -> gated on the flag read once: 1.015/1.010/1.013; (4) l2 penalty gradient no longer computes the unused penalty value (34 f64 divs + the all-zero fallback that needs a non-finite clipped w): ~neutral (0.99 median, 1.01-1.04 mean), kept as dead-code removal. RETRO n=1 checks for the rule: iter36 1.072, iter37 1.041 (vs paired 1.086: the second thread gains less alone, still clearly positive). cand .pyd cb029679, champ bfb87d05.

summary: Curve mix as sigmoid (one exp fewer) + exact kernel, plan, penalty, Adam trims
comment: ACCEPTED, 3b PRECISION-TRADE (NOT bit-for-bit: 50/50 param diffs from the sigmoid part only; mean LogLoss 0.3083203 -> 0.3083169, delta -3.4e-6, in band, |delta| < 1e-4 so no equal-wall-clock analysis needed).
